lead: An adder is the first combinational circuit that does arithmetic with bits. Adding two bits gives a sum bit and a carry bit, and both are Boolean functions: sum is XOR, carry is AND. A half adder computes this for two bits but cannot accept a carry from a lower bit. A full adder adds three bits, and chaining full adders gives a multi-bit adder. A BCD adder adds decimal digits stored as 4-bit codes and corrects the result. Adders sit inside processors, calculators, timers, digital clocks and address counters.
prereq: You need 5.2 for XOR and AND gates, 5.3 for writing the correction condition, and 5.1 for BCD codes.

sections.h3: Half adder: two bits in, sum and carry out

blocks.text: A half adder adds two input bits A and B. It produces a sum bit S and a carry bit C. The carry is 1 only when both inputs are 1, because 1 + 1 is 10 in binary: sum 0, carry 1.
The Boolean equations are S = A ⊕ B and C = A·B. The symbol ⊕ is XOR: it gives 1 when the inputs differ. The dot is AND.

The limitation is the missing carry input. When several bits are added, each column may receive a carry from the column on its right. A half adder cannot accept that carry, so it works only for the least significant column.

sections.h3: Full adder and the ripple-carry adder

blocks.text: A full adder adds three bits: A, B and C<sub>in</sub>. C<sub>in</sub> is the carry coming from the previous lower column. The outputs are sum S and carry C<sub>out</sub>.
S = A ⊕ B ⊕ C<sub>in</sub>;  C<sub>out</sub> = A·B + C<sub>in</sub>·(A ⊕ B)
blocks.where: A and B are input bits; C<sub>in</sub> is the input carry; S is the sum bit; C<sub>out</sub> is the output carry; ⊕ is XOR, · is AND, + is OR.

blocks.text: Build it from two half adders and one OR gate. Half adder 1 adds A and B: S<sub>1</sub> = A ⊕ B, C<sub>1</sub> = A·B. Half adder 2 adds S<sub>1</sub> and C<sub>in</sub>: S = S<sub>1</sub> ⊕ C<sub>in</sub>, C<sub>2</sub> = S<sub>1</sub>·C<sub>in</sub>. The OR gate gives C<sub>out</sub> = C<sub>1</sub> + C<sub>2</sub>. The OR is needed because a carry may come from either half adder. Dropping it loses a carry.

A 4-bit ripple-carry adder chains four full adders. Bit 0 adds the least significant bits and produces a carry into bit 1. Bit 1 adds its bits plus that carry, and so on. The final carry out is the fifth sum bit.
The carry must pass through every stage in turn, so the worst-case delay grows with the number of bits. This is why wide adders use faster carry circuits.

sections.h3: BCD adder and the correction step

blocks.text: A BCD digit uses four bits for decimal 0 to 9. The patterns 1010 to 1111 are invalid as BCD digits. When two BCD digits are added with a 4-bit binary adder, the raw sum can land in 10 to 19. It then needs correction.

Add 0110 (decimal 6) when the raw 4-bit sum is above 9 or when the adder gives a carry out. Adding 6 skips the six invalid codes and pushes the result into the next decimal digit. Let S<sub>3</sub>, S<sub>2</sub>, S<sub>1</sub>, S<sub>0</sub> be the raw sum bits, with S<sub>3</sub> the 8's bit. The correction signal is C<sub>corr</sub> = C<sub>out</sub> + S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>2</sub> + S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>1</sub>. Here S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>2</sub> means S<sub>3</sub> AND S<sub>2</sub>, and + means OR. If C<sub>corr</sub> = 1, add 0110 to the raw sum.

The carry-out case matters. For 9 + 9, the raw sum is 1 0010. The low nibble 0010 is below 10, but C<sub>out</sub> = 1. Correction gives 0010 + 0110 = 1000, so the answer is 1 1000 in BCD, decimal 18.

figure.caption: A full adder built from two half adders and an OR gate. For the bit where A = 1, B = 1 and C<sub>in</sub> = 0, the first half adder makes S<sub>1</sub> = 0 and C<sub>1</sub> = 1, the second makes S = 0 and C<sub>2</sub> = 0, and the OR gate gives C<sub>out</sub> = 1.

spec.title: Full adder from two half adders
spec.aria: A vertical block flow in which half adder 1 receives A=1 and B=1, sends S1=0 to half adder 2 and C1=1 to the OR gate, half adder 2 sends C2=0 to the OR gate and gives sum S=0, and the OR gate gives carry out 1.

examples.question: Add the 4-bit binary numbers 1011 and 0110 with a 4-bit ripple-carry adder. Then add the BCD digits 6 and 5 with a BCD adder. Show every carry and the correction.
steps: Label the bits from right to left: 1011 has A<sub>3</sub>A<sub>2</sub>A<sub>1</sub>A<sub>0</sub> = 1 0 1 1; 0110 has B<sub>3</sub>B<sub>2</sub>B<sub>1</sub>B<sub>0</sub> = 0 1 1 0. Start with C<sub>in</sub> = 0 at bit 0.
Bit 0: 1 + 0 + 0 = 1, so S<sub>0</sub> = 1 and carry into bit 1 is 0.
Bit 1: 1 + 1 + 0 = 2 = 10<sub>2</sub>, so S<sub>1</sub> = 0 and carry into bit 2 is 1.
Bit 2: 0 + 1 + 1 = 2 = 10<sub>2</sub>, so S<sub>2</sub> = 0 and carry into bit 3 is 1.
Bit 3: 1 + 0 + 1 = 2 = 10<sub>2</sub>, so S<sub>3</sub> = 0 and final carry C<sub>out</sub> = 1.

The sum bits are S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>2</sub>S<sub>1</sub>S<sub>0</sub> = 0001 and C<sub>out</sub> = 1, so the binary result is 1 0001<sub>2</sub> = 17. Check: 1011<sub>2</sub> = 11 and 0110<sub>2</sub> = 6, and 11 + 6 = 17.

BCD: 6 = 0110 and 5 = 0101. The 4-bit binary adder gives 0110 + 0101 = 1011, decimal 11. Here S<sub>3</sub>=1, S<sub>2</sub>=0, S<sub>1</sub>=1, C<sub>out</sub>=0, so C<sub>corr</sub> = S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>1</sub> = 1; the raw sum is above 9 and needs correction.
Add 0110 to 1011: 1011 + 0110 = 1 0001. The corrected low digit is 0001 and the carry to the next BCD digit is 1, so the two BCD digits are 0001 0001, decimal 11.
examples.answer: The binary sum is 1 0001<sub>2</sub> = 17, and the BCD result is 0001 0001 = 11.
examples.check:
def ripple(x, y, bits=4):
    carry = 0
    out = 0
    for i in range(bits):
        a = (x >> i) & 1
        b = (y >> i) & 1
        t = a + b + carry
        s = t & 1
        carry = t >> 1
        out |= s << i
    return out, carry

s, c = ripple(0b1011, 0b0110)
print((c << 4) | s)

def bcd_add(n1, n2):
    raw = n1 + n2
    low = raw & 0xF
    carry = raw >> 4
    if carry or low > 9:
        low += 6
        if low > 15:
            low &= 0xF
            carry += 1
    return carry * 10 + low

print(bcd_add(6, 5))

traps: Building a full adder from two half adders but forgetting the OR gate, so C<sub>1</sub> or C<sub>2</sub> is lost and the carry is wrong.
Applying BCD correction only for raw sums 1010 to 1111 and ignoring C<sub>out</sub>; 9 + 9 = 1 0010 needs correction even though the low nibble 0010 is below 10.
Confusing the binary carry weight 2 with the BCD correction value 0110, decimal 6. The correction is not decimal 10.
Trying to chain half adders directly for multi-bit addition; a half adder has no C<sub>in</sub>, so every column except the first needs a full adder.
Forgetting that the correction adder can itself produce a carry, as in 6 + 5, where 1011 + 0110 becomes 1 0001.

quiz.q: State the two Boolean outputs of a half adder for inputs A and B.
quiz.a: S = A ⊕ B and C = A·B.

quiz.q: Why does a full adder built from two half adders need an OR gate?
quiz.a: The two half adders produce two possible carries, C<sub>1</sub> = A·B and C<sub>2</sub> = (A⊕B)·C<sub>in</sub>. Either can be 1, so C<sub>out</sub> = C<sub>1</sub> + C<sub>2</sub>; an OR gate combines them.

quiz.q: Add 1001 and 0110 with a 4-bit ripple-carry adder. Give the sum bits and carry out.
quiz.a: Bit 0: 1+0=1, carry 0. Bit 1: 0+1=1, carry 0. Bit 2: 0+1=1, carry 0. Bit 3: 1+0=1, carry 0. Sum = 1111, C<sub>out</sub> = 0.

quiz.q: A BCD adder adds 8 (1000) and 7 (0111). Give the raw sum, the correction signal, and the final BCD result.
quiz.a: Raw sum = 1000 + 0111 = 1111 (15). S<sub>3</sub>=1, S<sub>2</sub>=1, S<sub>1</sub>=1, so S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>2</sub> = 1 and C<sub>corr</sub> = 1. Add 0110: 1111 + 0110 = 1 0101. Final: carry 1 and low digit 0101, decimal 15.

quiz.q: For a raw BCD sum 1101, evaluate C<sub>corr</sub> = C<sub>out</sub> + S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>2</sub> + S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>1</sub> and state whether correction is needed.
quiz.a: S<sub>3</sub>=1, S<sub>2</sub>=1, S<sub>1</sub>=0, C<sub>out</sub>=0. S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>2</sub>=1 and S<sub>3</sub>S<sub>1</sub>=0, so C<sub>corr</sub>=1. 1101 is 13, above 9, so add 0110: 1101+0110=1 0011, giving carry 1 and digit 0011.

quiz.q: Why does the worst-case delay of a 4-bit ripple-carry adder grow with the number of bits?
quiz.a: Each full adder cannot produce its final sum and carry until its C<sub>in</sub> is settled. The carry from bit 0 must pass through bit 1, then bit 2, then bit 3, so delay accumulates along the chain.

quiz.q: Which decimal values are invalid as a single BCD digit, and which 4-bit pattern is added as correction?
quiz.a: 1010 to 1111, decimal 10 to 15, are invalid. Add 0110, decimal 6, when correction is needed.

beyond: Not for the exam. Real processors use carry-lookahead or prefix adders to compute carries in parallel, trading more gates for less delay. BCD adders still appear in digital clocks, energy meters and seven-segment displays that must show decimal digits. A classic medium-scale IC is the 4-bit binary full adder, and FPGAs implement adders in dedicated carry chains. Search next for carry-lookahead adder, carry-select adder and binary-coded decimal arithmetic.
